# Cyber Insurance Central

> Carrier requirements, coverage comparisons, and underwriting insight for cyber insurance buyers. No carrier or broker sponsorship, no affiliate arrangements.

This site exists because cyber insurance is priced on security posture, not policy language, and most buyers don't have anyone in the room who can evaluate both. Content is written from the security side of the purchase: what carriers actually require before they'll write a policy, what a policy actually covers once sublimits and exclusions are read past the cover page, and who inside a buying organization needs to be involved so a claim doesn't get denied over a control gap nobody caught.

Content is written for the buying committee as a whole: CISOs and security teams who need to produce evidence, not just attestation; CFOs and risk managers who own the purchase and the broker relationship; and general counsel who need to read exclusions and breach-notification language before a policy is signed.

## About

- [About This Site](/about/): Who writes Cyber Insurance Central and why it carries no carrier or broker sponsorship

## Landscape

- [Cyber Insurance Landscape](/landscape/): Market structure, who buys cyber insurance inside an organization, and where the market stands
- [Coverage Components](/landscape/coverage-components/): What a cyber policy actually covers, first-party and third-party, and where sublimits and exclusions quietly cap what it pays
- [Underwriting Requirements](/landscape/underwriting-requirements/): The core security controls carriers now require before writing a policy at a competitive rate, and why attestation is no longer enough
- [Current Market Conditions](/landscape/market-conditions/): Where cyber insurance pricing and underwriting stand right now, reviewed quarterly
- [Carriers & MGAs](/landscape/carriers/): An independent, unranked index of active cyber insurance carriers and MGAs, including segment fit and structural notes

## Guides

- [Who Should Be in the Room](/guides/who-should-be-in-the-room/): Cyber insurance purchasing is usually CFO-owned, not CISO-owned. Who actually needs a seat at the table, and why the gap costs buyers coverage
- [How to Compare Cyber Insurance Quotes](/guides/how-to-compare-cyber-insurance-quotes/): A CISO's guide to what to actually check when comparing quotes, beyond what a broker-oriented comparison covers
- [Evidence Collection and Packaging](/guides/evidence-collection-and-packaging/): A vendor-neutral walkthrough of what real evidence looks like across the seven categories carriers actually ask about
- [What Changes at Renewal](/guides/renewal-leverage/): How a track record, control improvements, and an already-built evidence package become real leverage at renewal
- [The Incident Response Panel](/guides/incident-response-panel/): Many cyber policies require pre-approved vendors for a claim to be covered, and how to get your own vendors approved in advance

## Tools

- [Evidence Package Builder](/tools/evidence-package-builder/): Track evidence status across the categories carriers actually ask about and generate a renewal-ready summary
- [Coverage Gap & Sublimit Visualizer](/tools/sublimit-visualizer/): See how much of a policy limit actually reaches ransomware, business interruption, and other loss types
- [Insurability Impact Checker](/tools/insurability-impact-checker/): Answer seven questions about current controls and see the likely underwriting impact before applying
